- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and model is forecasting downward, reverse the trend direction if price has not yet fallen below 3-day low.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30-day moving average, apply mean reversion bias: adjust forecast to 85% of prior 30-day average + 15% of recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4), model often overfits short-term noise; use 14-day exponential smoothing to dampen erratic swings.
- If true outcome is below 75% of model forecast for 3 consecutive days, assume model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 5–10% and add 1–2% downward bias for next 5 days.
